habitat: Pairs, mainly in montane forest in the eastern regions, feeding in the upper and mid strata. They join bird parties in winter.
summary: An uncommon, localised resident. The male has a black forehead and facial mask, with no eyebrow, reaching the base of the bill, and an extensive orange wash from throat to belly. The vent is yellow and the upperparts are olive-green, with a grey cap. The female is less orange below and has a grey head and mantle. The call is a repetitive oo-poo. No openly licensed research-grade photo was found in the Kruger box. The Kemp code NB was left unchanged.

similar.note: Olive Bush-Shrike has a black mask that does not reach the base of the bill. A female Black-fronted Bush-shrike has a grey head and mantle.

calls.description: A repetitive oo-poo, like doh-me on the tonic sol-fa scale. Grade A call from Chama forest, Meru, Tanzania. The filename is XC703355-bushx bou,chama1112.mp3 and does not name the species. It was the only openly licensed grade A recording.
